'''Peter J. Braam''' is a Dutch-American computer scientist, mathematician and entrepreneur known for his contributions to large-scale computing systems. He has held academic positions at the [[University of Utah]], the [[University of Oxford]] and [[Carnegie Mellon University]]. Braam is recognized for creating the Lustre parallel file system, used in high-performance computing (HPC) environments.{{cn|date=June 2025}} 

== Early life and education ==
Braam was born in [[Utrecht]], Netherlands. He completed his undergraduate studies at [[Utrecht University]] in 1984.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} He pursued doctoral research under the supervision of [[Sir Michael Atiyah]] at the [[University of Oxford]], earning his DPhil in 1987 with a thesis titled ''Magnetic Monopoles and Hyperbolic Three-manifolds''.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Braam|first1=Peter J.|date=1987|title=Magnetic Monopoles and Hyperbolic Three-manifolds|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qflRHQAACAAJ|language=en|publisher=University of Oxford|access-date=March 19, 2019}}</ref>

== Academic career ==

Following his doctorate, Braam became a Junior Research Fellow at [[Merton College, Oxford]], and a C&C Huygens Fellow of the Netherlands Science Foundation.<ref name="merton">{{cite news|url=https://www.merton.ox.ac.uk/news/braam-bequest-enable-use-research-improve-countless-lives|title=Braam Bequest to enable the use of research to improve countless lives.|date=February 21, 2018|work=www.merton.ox.ac.uk|access-date=March 19, 2019}}</ref>

From 2013 to 2018, Braam has collaborated with the [[University of Cambridge]] on the [[Square Kilometre Array]] radio telescope project, focusing on data-intensive computing challenges. He has also served as a consultant to partners in the founding committee of Horizon 2020<ref>{{cite web |title=High-Performance Computing (HPC) |url=https://ec.europa.eu/programmes/horizon2020/en/h2020-section/high-performance-computing-hpc |website=Horizon 2020 - European Commission |access-date=March 19, 2019 |language=en |date=April 2, 2014}}</ref>{{failed verification|date=June 2025}} and the [[European Processor Initiative]]. 

At the [[University of Oxford]] he has been a Visiting Professor in the Department of Physics since 2019, and a visiting research fellow in mathematics since 2025, and a visiting professor of computer science at [[Waseda University]] since 2022.{{cn|date=June 2025}}

== Philanthrophy ==
Braam has endowed the Peter J. Braam Junior Research Fellowship and Graduate Scholarship in Human Wellbeing at [[Merton College, Oxford]]. These initiatives support early-career researchers and contribute to studies aimed at improving human wellbeing.<ref name="merton" />
